object_description: compact transparent rectangular building volume with a layered access perimeter
design_condition: The small-footprint volume is placed parallel to the main street, with a respectful setback creating arrival and restaurant space while differentiated open space continues the adjacent gardens and green slope.

positive.statement: The compact and transparent volume conveys openness and integrates subtly into the delicate urban setting.

position.rationale: The compact rectangular enclosure and transparent layered perimeter are clearly visible across the views.

positive.statement: Slight distortions establish subtle references to the surrounding urban context and emphasize transitions.

position.rationale: Slightly distorted perimeter lines visibly mark transitions along the otherwise regular volume.

positive.statement: Audience-oriented uses benefit from generous outdoor spaces and contribute to urban life.

position.rationale: Layered access edges and open perimeter space are most apparent along the southern approach.

positive.statement: The open-space design responds differently and precisely to the surrounding urban situations.

position.rationale: Several perimeter zones surround the compact footprint, though their specific urban situations are not labeled.

positive.statement: The generous column grid and connected areas enable a high degree of flexibility.

position.rationale: Regular vertical and horizontal point spacing visibly supports a repeated structural grid.

positive.statement: The inner courtyard supports natural lighting and ventilation of adjoining teaching rooms.

position.rationale: A distinct internal opening is visible near the lower central portion of the plan.

positive.statement: The project remains within the expected construction-cost specifications.

position.rationale: Cost performance has no useful spatial referent in the sampled geometry.

negative.statement: The project loses some of its radical lightness and transparency during the cleanup stage.

position.rationale: The compact envelope is visible, but cleanup-stage loss of transparency cannot be directly distinguished.

negative.statement: Removing much of the external access layer weakens the clear typological structure.

position.rationale: The layered perimeter and arrival edge are visible around the lower side of the compact plan.

negative.statement: The delivery ramp cuts through the open space, and the roof is difficult to use because of the photovoltaic systems.

position.rationale: The external access perimeter is visible, while ramp and photovoltaic equipment are not separately identifiable.

negative.statement: The proposed courtyard size is questionable.

position.rationale: The internal opening is visible, allowing approximate placement but not definitive program dimensions.

negative.statement: The floor-by-floor separation of teaching and research limits interdisciplinary exchange and flexibility.

position.rationale: The layered multi-level volume permits a broad interior anchor, but uses are not externally distinguishable.

negative.statement: The high usage density is perceived as squat and insufficiently open.

position.rationale: The compact, densely sampled enclosure supports the criticized squat spatial reading.

negative.statement: The extensive glazing conflicts with sustainability requirements and may compromise daylight in some interior areas.

position.rationale: Dense regular facade sampling indicates extensive glazing, though daylight effects remain unobservable.

negative.statement: The architectural expression loses sharpness and conciseness through the stronger horizontal facade structure and loss of the two-storey facade.

position.rationale: Strong horizontal bands are clearly visible across the elevations.

negative.statement: Not all usage arrangements and processes work smoothly.

position.rationale: The overall building is spatially anchored, but operational processes are not represented by exterior points.

negative.statement: Sustainability and building technology require further optimization for certification.

position.rationale: Certification and technology optimization have no reliable spatial referent in the sampled geometry.
